title: Opaque export manifest pagination and resumable downloads
creator: Hannah Lee
description: Customers requesting large historical consumption snapshots (multi-GB to TB) hit reliability and UX problems when a single export manifest references thousands of signed objects. Current delivery creates a monolithic manifest and a single transfer process which is brittle for mobile clients, slow connections, and webhook consumers that must rehydrate the whole dataset. This ticket designs and implements a paginated, opaque manifest API plus lightweight resumable download semantics: manifests are returned in pages (with opaque page tokens), each page contains a small list of signed URLs and checksums, and the download itself can be resumed from the last-acked page. For webhook deliveries we deliver page-level webhooks so receivers can process incrementally rather than waiting for a final signal. The approach reduces memory pressure in the exporter, enables partial retries, simplifies client-sdk implementation, and improves observability for per-page transfer success/failure. Security considerations include short-lived signatures, strict page token verification, and audit logging. Migration path will support both old monolithic manifests and the new paginated manifests and provide a transitional flag per-tenant.
acceptance_criteria: API: GET /exports/:id/manifest returns paginated results with opaque page_token and next_page_token; schema version header present
Resumability: clients can POST /exports/:id/ack-page with page_token to mark successful receipt, exporter will resume from first un-acked page
S3: each paginated page contains pre-signed URLs with per-object checksum and size; signatures expire within configured TTL
Webhooks: for webhook delivery mode, the system sends page-level webhook callbacks and supports backoff/retry semantics per page
Observability: per-page metrics emitted (page_bytes, page_objects, page_duration, page_errors) and dashboard added in Console
Backward compatibility: tenants without migration flag still receive the original monolithic manifest until migration window ends
tasks: Design API contract and manifest schema (include versioning plan)
Implement paginated manifest generator in exporter service with streaming page flush
Add page-ack endpoint and persistence of ack state per export/tenant
Modify S3 signer to generate short TTL per object and include checksum metadata
Implement page-level webhook sender with idempotency and per-page retry policy
Update Console UI to show export progress by page and add per-page metrics
Add E2E tests (large export simulation, intermittent network, resume flow)
Run migration rollouts with feature flag and monitor key SLOs for 2 weeks
